blocks.text: An attempted visit to a sick friend (second or third century ad):
ad amicum nostrum Lucium; visitemus eum.
blocks.speaker: marcus

blocks.text: non longe; si vis, ambula. (after a short walk) haec est, puto, domus eius. haec est.
blocks.speaker: marcus

blocks.text: ecce ianitor; interroga illum num possimus intrare et videre amicum nostrum.
blocks.speaker: gaius

blocks.text: dominum tuum Lucium; de salute eius venimus.
blocks.speaker: marcus

blocks.text: dominum tuum volumus visitare. si vigilat, nuntia nos.
blocks.speaker: marcus

blocks.text: gratulamur illi. cum venerit, dic illi nos ad eum venisse de salute eius gratulantes, quia omnia bona sunt.
blocks.speaker: marcus

blocks.text: Vocabulary (in order of first appearance; words that appear more than once are in bold)

rows: intrā paucōs diēs ‘a few days ago’
incurrō (like currō) ‘fall ill’ (here a present where we would expect a past, because Latin uses the present for an action that began in the past but continues in the present)
cum vēnerit ‘when he comes’ (see chapter 47.2 for the construction)
grātulantēs is a present participle of

blocks.text: A very unrealistic representation of how a lawyer finds a job (perhaps third century ad). Because many people who learned Latin did so in order to become lawyers, ancient Latin teachers painted a rosy picture of the life of a lawyer in an effort to encourage people to study Latin.
r i c h f r i en d : domine, salve.
salvus sis semper, amice. r i c h f r i en d : quomodo sunt res tuae? omnia bene?
blocks.speaker: lawyer

blocks.text: quomodo dei volunt. r i c h f r i en d : quid nunc agis?
blocks.speaker: lawyer

blocks.text: agebam, nunc autem vacat mihi. r i c h f r i en d : volo tibi iniungere administrationem meae actionis. eamus; ambula et ego tibi dabo quod agas. omnium enim bonorum dignus es.
blocks.speaker: lawyer

blocks.text: Vocabulary (in order of first appearance; words that appear more than once are in bold, and those in bold in the preceding vocabulary list are omitted)

rows: agēbam ‘I was doing things’ (imperfect tense of agō)
quod agās ‘something for you to do’
autem ‘however’ (translate one word earlier than where it appears in Latin)
enim ‘for’ (in the sense of ‘because’; translate one word earlier than where it appears in Latin)
vacat mihi ‘I don’t have anything to do’

blocks.text: Come with me in order to see Lucius.
blocks.speaker: marcus

blocks.text: Let’s go. Where does he live?
blocks.speaker: gaius

blocks.text: He lives here; this is his house.
blocks.speaker: marcus

blocks.text: We are seeking your master. We have heard that our friend Lucius is ill and we want to see him: is he awake?
blocks.speaker: marcus

blocks.text: Lucius does not live here; my master’s name is Titus. PART III
